ServerOptions.PublicHost: Address the client is told to connect to (server list gate addresses). Must be an IP literal.
ServerOptions.BindAddress: Interface the HTTP and gate ports listen on. Empty: loopback when PublicHost is a loopback address (local play and the tests: no Windows Firewall prompt per test host), otherwise every interface.
ServerOptions.ReconstructedDungeons: Story dungeons whose encounter scripts are not in the client use the reconstructed waves in Reconstructed/dungeon-monsters.json (inferred, marked "odtworzone"); off refuses them as before.
ServerOptions.Ro1AggressiveMonsters: Field monsters whose Ragnarok Online 1 counterpart is aggressive (rAthena pre-renewal mob_db, listed in Reconstructed/ro1-aggressive-monsters.json) attack on sight like the client's AIConfig 20000004 monsters. An RO1 reference, not client evidence (inferred); on by default as a trial (owner's decision, 28.10), off changes nothing.
ServerOptions.Ro1AggressiveMaxLevelGap: The RO1 aggression stays off for a monster on an open field (not a dungeon, town or sandbox) whose own field spawns hold a common monster (MonsterService.Ro1GateMinSharePercent of the population) more than this many levels below it (Payon Forest: Greatest General 55 and Elder Willow 34 among Horns 16), so new characters can follow the story there; bosses and MVPs are never gated; 0 or negative: no gate. (inferred, owner's decision 31.10)
ServerOptions.Ro1MonsterHp: Monsters whose Ragnarok Online 1 counterpart is much tougher than the client makes them get the RO1 HP (Reconstructed/ro1-monster-hp.json: the Pupa, 4 HP in the client, 427 here). An RO1 reference, not client evidence (inferred). Off by default: the client cuts their HP on purpose (_kAttriScale), so the 1:1 server keeps it; an operator who wants the RO1 feel turns it on.
ServerOptions.PetWorldFollower: A pet in the active setup plan walks beside its owner as a type-7 world unit (PetFollowerService). Off by default: the client shows a deployed pet only in its guardian skill (LC_Scene_Sync._useInSkill, petConfigId, a local model effect), and its only follower, PendantType.PetFollow, has no PendantConfig row while LC_PetHelper.IsFollowPet returns false. The projection is (inferred), kept for an operator who wants the pet visible.
ServerOptions.TrafficLog: Game-message JSON log (data/logs/traffic-*.jsonl): "off", "on" or a comma-separated account list. Formatting and writes run off the game loop; keep it off for load tests and production.
ServerOptions.PreloadGameData: Parse all client config tables before the gates open (tools/run-server.ps1 turns it on). Off by default so the hundreds of short-lived test hosts load only the tables they touch.
ServerOptions.GameDataDir: Folder with the data exported from the client: config/ (tools/ConfigExport), sceneeditor/ and nav/ (tools/WorldData); default DataDir.
ServerOptions.WalkCheck: Walk check (SceneService.AcceptWalkAsync): the distance budget of the speed attribute and the client's nav grid. "enforce" (default) snaps a refused walk back to the last good position, "log" only reports it (CheatMonitor), "off" skips the check. A walk to a position that is not a number is refused in every mode but "off".
ServerOptions.TravelCheck: Travel check (SceneService.Travel): which raw 30012 and 30131 requests a client may send. "enforce" (default) refuses the others, "log" counts them and lets them through (CheatMonitor), "off" skips the check.
ServerOptions.AntiCheat: Anti-cheat limits and the web panel's suspicious-activity thresholds (CheatMonitor, docs/systems/anticheat.md).
ServerOptions.AreaName: The server (area) inside the cluster: the login screen shows the cluster name above it.
ServerOptions.StallNameMaxLength: Stall title limit in characters. The original's PublicParamConfig.StallsNameCharacterLimit (10) was sized for Chinese; English titles need more. ClientHooks.LuaPatches sets the client's input limit to the same value.
ServerOptions.PlayBook: The live season playbook (SeasonService). 101 is the only one this client has season content for; a value set in game with "!season" overrides it.
ServerOptions.SeasonStart: The season's first day, yyyy-MM-dd; empty means the server's first start (kept in the database).
ServerOptions.OpenContent: Owner policy (2026-10-11): every piece of content the client can show is playable. Off by default so the tests keep pinning the original's rules; appsettings.json turns it on for the real server.
ServerOptions.Pass: Battle pass policy: the premium track is free for now.
ServerOptions.Shop: Paid products and top-ups: free for now (owner decision 2026-10-31).
ServerOptions.GmAccounts: Accounts allowed to use GM commands in game ("!" lines in chat, the client's GM panel, 1031/1034). Empty: GmOpenWhenEmpty decides. docs/guide/gm-access.md.
ServerOptions.GmOpenWhenEmpty: What an empty GmAccounts means in game: true = every account has GM (research server, tests, local play), false = nobody has GM. Left unset, ServerHost decides: true only on a server that only this machine reaches (LocalOnly) and that was not set to Production explicitly (ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT, DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT or --environment); false on a public bind, behind a proxy, or in Production. The loopback HTTP POST /ro3emu/gm (the operator's tools) keeps the old rule either way: empty = every account.
ServerOptions.Panel: The web control panel on its own port (docs/guide/panel.md).
ServerOptions.Updates: The web panel's update manager (Updates.UpdateManager, docs/guide/panel.md).
ServerOptions.ReceiptRetention: How long economic receipts keep their payload and outcome bytes (ReceiptRetention).
ServerOptions.LoginAttemptsPerMinute: Credential checks (SDK login, character deletion) one remote address may make per minute; past it the server answers 429 without hashing. Each check costs a 100 000-round PBKDF2 hash, and logins register accounts. Loopback is exempt (local play, the load tests, RO3Emu.exe); behind a reverse proxy every player shares the proxy's address, so raise this there.
ServerOptions.LoginLimitIncludesLoopback: Tests: the credential limit and the gift code address limit apply to loopback too.
ServerOptions.OperatorToken: The operator token the loopback tools (/ro3emu/gm, /shutdown, /online, /reports, /metrics) must send in X-Ro3Emu-Operator (Http.OperatorToken). Unset: a random one, kept in DataDir/operator.token. Set (at least 32 characters): this one, also written to that file, for scripts that already hold a secret.
ServerOptions.RefuseUnknownAccounts: A game login (SDK login) with an account name that has no account is refused instead of creating the account, so accounts come only from the web panel's sign-up (a closed test). The client shows its wrong-credentials popup, as for a wrong password. Off: the first login creates the account, as before.
ServerOptions.ChatFlood: Chat flood protection (ChatService.Flood.cs). Off by default.
ServerOptions.GiftCodeAttemptsPerMinute: Gift code attempts (POST /gift-card/use/v2, docs/systems/gift-codes.md) one remote address, and separately one account, may make per minute; past it the server answers the refusal code GiftCardRateLimited without looking the code up. Loopback is exempt from the address budget, as for LoginAttemptsPerMinute, but not from the account budget. Behind a reverse proxy every player shares the proxy's address, so raise this there.
ServerOptions.Voice: Team voice relay proof of concept (Voice/, docs TBD). Off until a port is set.
ServerOptions.GuildBlockedWords: (inferred) Locally configured text blocklist; the original service's sensitive-word dictionary is unavailable.
ServerOptions.GuildFounding: "responders" (as the client says): a guild costs GuildCreateCostShow and is founded through GuildResponsePeopleLimit responders within GuildResponseTimeLimit, or the founder gets the cost back by mail; the create widget's toggle only waives the founder's approval of each response. "instant": a host's shortcut, a guild is free and Normal at once.
ServerOptions.GuildLeagueMinMembers: Guild League registration's membership threshold. Unset: GuildSettingConfig GuildLeaguePeopleNum (40, read as the "Guild membership reaches ${1}" requirement, inferred). A small realm or a test can lower it.
ServerOptions.ReconnectGraceSeconds: Seconds an in-game role stays in the world after its game socket drops, waiting for the client's silent reconnect (Phonest ConnectServerReq ReConnection). 60 is the reference AVATAR_LOSE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; it must exceed the client's 20 s + 10 s budgets. 0 turns grace off.
ServerOptions.ChickenTestPlayers: TEST AID, not original behaviour: Survivor Battle (match entry 2) starts with this many entrants in teams of ChickenTestTeamSize instead of EatChickenMatchConfig's 100 in teams of 5 (the client gives no sign of server-side filler bots). 0 keeps the config. GM "!chicken shape" sets the same in memory.
ServerOptions.RaidPreparationSeconds: (inferred) Seconds of a Realm of the Gods raid's preparation phase: the boss waits until the team leader presses the scene's "Start Battle" button (DungeonLua_30201xx DungeonBase.FunctionButtons, sent as 30125) or this time runs out. The client has the button, not the phase length.
ServerOptions.ScriptedScenePacePercent: Pace of the scripted scenes' own timers (the hide-and-seek rounds), in percent of their reconstructed length: 100 plays them as designed, a test makes them shorter.
ServerOptions.SpawnLimits: Fewer of one monster on one map (Ro3Emu:SpawnLimits). Empty by default: every spawn pool group creates as many as the client's own scene data says (docs/systems/monster-ai.md). A rule only lowers the count a pool group rolls for its NPC at the first spawn of a map line; respawns replace each defeated monster one for one.
ServerOptions.FieldExpRates: More (or less) EXP from the monsters of the open field, by the killer's base level (Ro3Emu:FieldExpRates). Empty by default: a kill pays what the client's drop tables say (docs/systems/monster-ai.md). The first rule whose level range holds the killer's level scales that kill's Base EXP, and the Job EXP that equals it, by its percent. (inferred: the original had no such knob.)
ServerOptions.Experience: Operator EXP tuning (inferred). Defaults preserve the exported tables and existing catch-up rules.
ServerOptions.StarCoreDrops: (inferred) Star Cores drop for roles with the Astral Level open (ParagonService.StarCoreDrops). The client data gives them no source; false turns the reconstructed drop off.
ServerOptions.LordsManePercent: (inferred) Chance in percent that an MVP kill drops a Lord's Mane, the Starshatter Dragon's unseal material, to one participant (MvpService). The client data gives it no source; 0 turns it off.
ServerOptions.TitleCrestPercent: (inferred) Chance in percent that a boss kill drops a title Crest of the boss level's tier (TitleService). The client data gives the Crests no source; 0 turns it off.
ServerOptions.TavernDayDrinks: (inferred) Every Tavern active day (20 minutes in a room) also brings one higher drink: Grape Wine every 7th active day, Craft Brew every 3rd, Gingerbread otherwise (TavernService). The client data gives only Hot Cocoa a source (the daily quest's award); false leaves it at that.
ServerOptions.RaidEnrageSeconds: (inferred) Seconds from a raid boss fight's start to its enrage, against which the Final Trial "more than N minutes remaining until enrage" honors (TenGameplayFinalTrialConfig, condition 7004) are judged. The enrage timer lives in the boss's server script, which the client does not carry.
ServerOptions.BossSkills: Boss special skills (BossSkillSets, MonsterService.BossSkills): the scheduler's inferred numbers.
ServerOptions.Testing: TEST AIDS, not original behaviour (Ro3Emu:Testing, docs/guide/hosting.md): To-Do activities open at any hour and rewards that never run out, so testers need not wait for a weekday or a weekly reset. All off by default; GM "!testing" changes them in memory.
TestingOptions.AlwaysOpen: Every To-Do activity (DailyActivityConfig) counts as open now, any weekday and hour: its occurrence repeats back to back with its own length, phases included. The Guild League and Territory Wars rows keep their calendars.
TestingOptions.UnlimitedRewards: Reward allowances and attempt counters never run out: dungeon reward counts (Realm of the Gods, Phantom Realm), MVP daily reward counts, the Commendation Vault extra awards and Dodo's Request.
BossSkillOptions.Enabled: Off: bosses only swing their normal attack, as before the scheduler.
BossSkillOptions.FirstCastDelayMs: Delay after a boss engages before its first special skill.
BossSkillOptions.GlobalCooldownMs: Pause after a special's action ends before the next one (the boss swings meanwhile); a row's longer _iPubCD wins.
BossSkillOptions.PlaceholderCooldownMs: Cooldown of a skill whose family carries only placeholder cooldowns (every row 0-2 s: Realm of the Gods, story Baphomet and Pharaoh), where the encounter script set the pace.
BossSkillOptions.PhaseHpPercents: HP percent at which a boss with phase variants enters each next phase (phase 1, phase 2...).
BossSkillOptions.DefaultRadius: Area radius (m) when neither the row nor its show template gives one.
BossSkillOptions.MaxReach: Longest distance (m) to its target at which a boss starts a targeted skill; rows with "anywhere" ranges (_iDistanceMax 9999) are capped to it.
BossSkillOptions.MaxHitsPerCast: Most hits one cast lands (a show's attack points; Ring of Light has three).
BossSkillOptions.DamagePercent: Boss skill damage as a percent of the row's formula result.
BossSkillOptions.SummonCount: Minions of a summon skill whose description gives no count.
BossSkillOptions.SummonLifeMs: Life of a summoned minion without a self-destruct born buff.
ReceiptRetentionOptions.Days: Age in days after which a receipt is compacted; 0 keeps every receipt whole. A compacted receipt still replays (by its intent hash), so the window only bounds how far back the offline audit re-checks intents.
ReceiptRetentionOptions.IntervalMinutes: Minutes between compaction runs (the first runs a few minutes after startup).
FeedbackOptions.MaxLength: Longest report text kept (characters); longer text is cut and marked truncated.
FeedbackOptions.ContextLines: Server log lines about the player stored with a report (RecentLogBuffer); 0 keeps none and leaves the buffer out of the logging pipeline.
FeedbackOptions.ContextMinutes: How far back those log lines may reach.
FeedbackOptions.CooldownSeconds: Minimum seconds between two reports of one account.
FeedbackOptions.DiscordWebhookUrl: A Discord channel webhook (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...): each stored report is also posted there. Unset keeps reports in the file only. The URL lets anyone post to that channel, so keep it out of committed config.
ChatFloodOptions.WindowSeconds: The window the two line budgets count in.
ChatFloodOptions.OpenLines: Lines per window on the open channels: world, map, recruitment and every other channel anyone can join.
ChatFloodOptions.PrivateLines: Lines per window on whispers, party, guild and friend-group chat, counted apart from the open channels.
ChatFloodOptions.DuplicateSeconds: A line whose text (letter case and spaces aside) went to the same channel or player this many seconds before is dropped; 0 turns the check off.
ChatFloodOptions.MuteSeconds: How long an account that went past a budget cannot chat.
UpdateOptions.Check: Ask GitHub for new releases: when the page asks and every CheckHours. Off: no request leaves the server and the page shows the installed version only.
UpdateOptions.Repository: The GitHub repository whose releases are offered (owner/name).
UpdateOptions.CheckHours: Hours between two checks in the background; at least 1.
UpdateOptions.ApiUrl: The GitHub API's address. Another one (a local copy of the releases list) is for testing; its own address may then serve the downloads too.
UpdateOptions.Hosting: How the server is run, which decides whether the page can install: auto (found from the environment), systemd, service (a Windows service wrapper that restarts it), docker, app (RO3Emu.exe or the launcher) or manual.
UpdateOptions.InstallDir: The release folder the server runs from (the one with server/ and RO3Emu). Empty: the folder above the server's own executable when it is a release's.
BackupOptions.Keep: Copies kept, compressed or not; older ones are deleted.
BackupOptions.Uncompressed: Newest copies left as plain .db files, ready to restore or open; at least 1. Set it to Keep to compress nothing.
BackupOptions.ReserveMegabytes: Disk space a backup leaves free for the live database to grow (inferred; server tuning). When a copy and this do not fit, the oldest copies go first (never the newest two), or the backup is skipped and logged as critical.
BackupOptions.BigDatabaseMegabytes: From this database size a restart makes no copy while the newest is younger than IntervalHours, and a scheduled copy is checked once per BigDatabaseCheckHours (inferred; server tuning). 0 turns this off.
BackupOptions.BigDatabaseCheckHours: Hours between integrity checks of scheduled copies on a big database.
VoiceOptions.Port: TCP port the voice gate listens on; 0 keeps the relay off.
VoiceOptions.MaxRoomSize: Members a single voice room (one party/team) may hold.
VoiceOptions.MaxTavernRoomSize: Listeners a Tavern room's voice may hold. The room itself takes PublicParamConfig.BarroomPersonNum (1000) members; (inferred) the relay bounds its own fan-out, everyone past this keeps the room's text chat.
VoiceOptions.FramesPerSecond: Audio frames a connection may send per second before the token bucket drops the extra ones.
VoiceOptions.Burst: Extra frames the token bucket allows in a short burst on top of FramesPerSecond.
VoiceOptions.ControlPerSecond: Control frames (Join, Leave, Mic, Speaker, Ping, anything else after Auth) a connection may send per second; the extra ones are dropped, and a sustained flood (3x this rate over 5 s) disconnects it. A real client sends a few per minute: a ping every 10 s plus the player's own clicks.
VoiceOptions.ControlBurst: Extra control frames allowed in a short burst on top of ControlPerSecond.
VoiceOptions.MaxPayload: Longest opus payload accepted in one Audio frame, in bytes.
VoiceOptions.TicketSeconds: How long a 77015 ticket stays valid before a connection must present it.
VoiceOptions.MaxConnections: Voice connections the listener accepts at once; past this new connections are refused.
VoiceOptions.MaxConnectionsPerIp: Voice connections one IP address may hold at once (a LAN party behind one router needs a few).
VoiceOptions.MaxFailedAuthPerIp: Connections from one IP that end without a valid Auth before that IP is refused for a minute.
VoiceOptions.FirstFrameTimeoutSeconds: Seconds a fresh connection has to send its Auth frame before it is closed. A test host lowers this.
VoiceOptions.IdleTimeoutSeconds: Seconds without any frame before an authed connection is closed as idle. A test host lowers this.
ShopOptions.FreeProducts: Products, packs and top-ups are granted without payment.
ShopOptions.FreeTopUpsPerDay: Free top-ups of one package a role may take per game day (inferred cap, at least 1).
PassOptions.FreePremium: Every role gets the premium track and its privileges without the premium item 703.
PassOptions.Play: Pass EXP from play: challenges, daily activity, monsters, dungeons, MVPs and story (NewActivityService.PassPlay).
OpenContentOptions.Functions: Functions the original never opened (base level 999/9999) whose client UI and data work: 7201 Realm War map, 70122 Totem Shop, 41 Feedback, 1000000 Adv. Guild (AdventureGroupService), 96 Valhalla Trials (ValhallaService), 69 Season page (SeasonPageService; level 50 until the 20 Oct 2026 client closed it with condition 2000062, [1002,9999]) (Feedback's panel comes from Ro3Emu.ClientHooks.FeedbackButton, its backend is FeedbackService), 14 Title (TitleService; its widget is hosted by Ro3Emu.ClientHooks.TitleButton). Shells without a working panel (Academy 34...) stay closed so the menu shows no dead buttons; a function joins this list together with its backend. Novice Challenge (90, activity 112) is left out (owner, 2026-10-11): its 15 random event texts are "Event Text..."/"Option A" filler and the first node's dialogues 9901-9904 do not exist, so the original never finished it.
OpenContentOptions.Activities: NewActivityConfig rows whose own open condition is a level the cap never reaches (e.g. 112 Novice Challenge). 200 Pass I asks for base level 99 (condition 21000019). Pass II (201, the same condition and EXP currency) opens after Pass I, when the owner adds it here.
OpenContentOptions.SeasonStageActivities: The season page's stage activities (MultiverseStage._kStageActivity of the playbook: for 101 that is 105 Fragment Gather, 106 Treasure, 107 Middle Season, 109/110 Racing, 111 World Exploration, 115 Emblem) are open whatever their own condition: every one is [1002,99], the final level cap (BaseLvLimitConfig day 198), so on a fresh realm the season page would list them all as locked for months. Their time windows still apply (107 keeps its settlement bounds, KeepTimeLimits), and World Exploration's chapters open with them (NewActivityService.WorldPhaseOpen).
OpenContentOptions.IgnoreServerDay: Server-day conditions (3031 open days, 3030 playbook seconds) count as met from the first day.
OpenContentOptions.PerpetualWindows: TimeLimitConfig windows bounded by the server opening or by season stages open at the server opening and never close (every such id has a single state row: card pools, passes, Novice Challenge, Battle for Prontera, tower races...). Windows of activities given by absolute dates that already passed repeat with their own length.
OpenContentOptions.KeepTimeLimits: Windows that keep their original bounds: 1021 Midterm Settlement, 1023 Top 10 Guilds, 1036 Feedback (settlements, not content).
OpenContentOptions.ClosedActivities: NewActivityConfig rows that stay closed: 1011-1014, the original's "Test ... Pool" rows.
OpenContentOptions.PerpetualAbsolute: Absolute windows that also become perpetual: 1060, the Territory War activity around the May block.
OpenContentOptions.TerritoryWarCycleDays: Territory Wars: the exported block of battles (2026-05-19..27, absolute dates) repeats every N days; 0 keeps the absolute dates. Each repeat is its own territory season (TerritoryWarsClock.Epoch), so rewards settle every cycle.
AntiCheatOptions.MessagesPerSecond: Game messages one session may send per second on average (any message); 0 turns the limit off. A walk goes out at every turn, so steering with the mouse can send dozens a second: the default leaves room for that.
AntiCheatOptions.MessageBurst: Game messages one session may send at once above that rate.
AntiCheatOptions.MessageLimits: Tighter budgets of single message ids, "msgId": "perSecond/burst": the ones whose work is large (a full role login, a database insert). Unset ids only share the session's budget. The burst covers the role screen's m_iMaxRoleNumber (6) slots, so filling every slot, or visiting every role through "switch character" (the same connection), never waits on the rate.
AntiCheatOptions.MicroRequests: Frames one micro gate connection may send once its account is bound, "perSecond/burst" (heartbeats are free). A login opens with a burst of friend, rank and user data calls; after that the client calls on clicks. Over budget a request is answered as refused without running.
AntiCheatOptions.MicroRequestsBeforeSign: The same before an account is bound: the client needs the key exchange and one verifySdk there. Over budget the connection is closed.
AntiCheatOptions.ChatLines: Chat lines (group channels and whispers) one session may send, "perSecond/burst".
AntiCheatOptions.ChatMaxLength: Characters of one chat line; longer lines are refused.
AntiCheatOptions.MaxRolesPerAccount: Roles one account may hold: LC_SelectRoleManager.m_iMaxRoleNumber (6), the role screen's slots.
AntiCheatOptions.FlushSeconds: Seconds between writes of the refusal counts to the database.
AntiCheatOptions.KeepDays: Days refusal counts and EXP samples are kept.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.WindowHours: The window the list looks back over, in hours.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.Refusals: Refused requests of one account in the window that list it.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.GainFactor: A character's gain in the window is listed when it is this many times the median gain of the characters that gained any in the same window, and at least the floor below.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.ZenyFloor: Zeny (currency 1) gained from the game (ledger sources) in the window, at least.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.ItemFloor: Items gained from the game (ledger sources, all items counted together) in the window, at least.
AntiCheatAlertOptions.ExpFloor: Base EXP gained in the window, at least.
ExperienceOptions.MonsterPercent: All monster Base EXP, after level, party and field adjustments; 100 = unchanged, 200 = double.
ExperienceOptions.JobFromBasePercent: Job EXP generated from Base EXP, in percent. Null uses PublicParamConfig.BaseToJobConversionPercent.
ExperienceOptions.CatchUpEnabled: Apply BaseExpAddConfig's catch-up bonus to monster kills and direct EXP grants.
ExperienceOptions.PartyBonusEnabled: Apply the existing party EXP bonus to monster rewards.
PanelOptions.Enabled: Serve the panel. Off: its port is not opened at all.
PanelOptions.Port: The panel's own HTTP port, next to the server's HttpPort.
PanelOptions.BindAddress: Interface the panel listens on. Empty: the one the server's other ports use (loopback for local play). A reverse proxy on the same machine sets 127.0.0.1 so only the proxy reaches the panel.
PanelOptions.PublicUrl: The panel's public address when players reach it some other way than the server's host and panel port, such as behind a reverse proxy (https://example.com:8443). The server announces it on GET /ro3emu/panel of its HTTP port, so a launcher that joined finds it. Empty: launchers look on the host's panel port.
PanelOptions.TrustedProxies: Addresses of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed: the client address for the login budget and https for the cookie's Secure flag. Empty: both headers are ignored, whoever sends them.
PanelOptions.SessionHours: Hours a panel login stays valid without use; each request extends it. Sessions live in memory and end when the server restarts.
PanelOptions.Registration: Accounts can be created on the panel's sign-up page. Off: only the game's first login creates them.
PanelOptions.SignUpsPerAddressPerDay: Accounts the sign-up creates for one client address (an IPv6 one by its /64 network) in any 24 hours; 0: no limit. The address is the connection's peer, or behind a proxy of TrustedProxies the one it forwards, so a reverse proxy must be listed there or every visitor shares its address.
PanelOptions.SignUpsPerHour: Accounts the sign-up creates in any hour, from every address together; 0: no limit.
PanelOptions.ImageDir: The folder of the pictures the pages show (item, monster, class and map images), decoded from the operator's own client by the data export. Empty: icons/ in the game data folder. Without it the pages draw letters instead.
PanelOptions.Branding: White-label branding: the server's own name, tagline, logo, footer and colour on every page.
PanelOptions.Roles: Staff roles of the admin area by account (as stored): Moderator, GM or Admin. Accounts of Ro3Emu:GmAccounts are Admins too. An Admin can add more roles from the panel; the ones listed here cannot be changed there.
PanelOptions.RequireAdmin2FA: GM and Admin accounts must turn on two-factor authentication before the admin area opens to them. Unset: on when other machines reach the server (ServerOptions.LocalOnly), off for local play. The server resolves it at start.
PanelOptions.LoginAddresses: Keep and show the address of each login in the login history. Off: only the time and the way in.
PanelBranding.ServerName: The name in the header, the title bar and the home page (at most 64 characters). Empty: Ro3Emu:ClusterName.
PanelBranding.Tagline: A line under the name on the home page (at most 160 characters).
PanelBranding.LogoPath: A PNG, JPG or WebP file in the server's data folder (a path relative to it), shown instead of the star.
PanelBranding.FooterText: The footer's text instead of RO3Emu's (at most 300 characters).
PanelBranding.AccentColor: The colour of links, focus rings and highlights, as #rrggbb.
